title: Beautiful Sacrifice
transcript: Sometimes the most beautiful wins [music] come from the simplest of positions. In this situation, black and white both have three pawns left and they're both trying to get a new queen as fast [music] as they can, but they need to be careful. After D5, E3, and D6, if black takes this pawn, now actually he would [music] lose on the spot because this would clear up the path for the C pawn and after C7, white would get a queen first and then checkmate on B7. So, actually black should just ignore this pawn and continue to run with the F pawn. And now white is in front of a pretty difficult choice. To take or not to take. And as it turns out, if white doesn't take and plays pawn to D7, now after both sides get a new queen, there is no way to get to the black king. Black can play, for example, queen to E5 and after white tries to sneak in and deliver the same checkmate that we saw, the king can actually collect the C pawn and at best this is going to be a draw. So, actually after pawn to E2, white should take the C pawn. And now both sides will get a new queen, but this time the white queen is also defending the C pawn. Not only that, white is threatening the checkmate on B7 and if black takes the pawn trying to give breathing room to the king, after queen to B7 anyway, either the black king is getting checkmated in just two moves or if it comes out, white is going to trade the queens and then promote another pawn way faster. But black is not that naive and there is a more resilient move to continue the game. Black has queen to E5 with a check to the white king, but white had foreseen this idea and he just covers the check with pawn to C7, now renewing the threat of queen to B7 checkmate. And after black covers the checkmate threat, which is the only [music] thing that he can do, white has a majestic move. You see, if only this pawn wasn't here, white could give a check on C7, force king A6, and then deliver a checkmate on A7. So, the only winning [music] move in this position is the brilliant queen A6 check. A beautiful [music] and elegant move that sacrifices the queen completely just to promote to a new queen. And after the king comes back, we are in the same situation. But the pawn is not there anymore. Which means that after queen C7 and king A6, queen to A7 [music] will be a beautiful checkmate.
